title: UC Irvine School of Education to lead $10 million national center on AI and postsecondary writing
snippet: UC Irvine's School of Education has been awarded a $10 million, five-year grant from the U.S. Department of Education's Institute of Education Sciences to establish the WRITE AI Center. The center will lead a national effort to examine how generative AI can strengthen college writing instruction without undermining students' writing, critical thinking, and communication skills.

title: MIT's Ad Hoc Committee on AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Research Training Releases Final Report
snippet: MIT's Ad Hoc Committee on AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Research Training released its final report, concluding that generative AI can credibly address almost any written undergraduate assignment. The report recommends shifting toward oral exams, process-based portfolios, and course-specific AI policies.
match_reason: websearch (publication) — This is a landmark, precedent-setting report by a peer research university (MIT) that directly addresses AI policy, academic integrity, and assessment redesign.

title: UC Berkeley announces new professional graduate degree in AI and machine learning
snippet: UC Berkeley will offer a Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (MAIML) starting in fall 2027, with applications opening Sept. 24, 2026. Offered by the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society, the curriculum spans data science, machine learning, probability, statistical inference, and AI ethics.
match_reason: websearch (press_release) — This represents a major new AI-focused graduate degree program at a flagship UC campus, incorporating AI ethics and responsible deployment.

title: Ithaka S+R Report Examines Gap in AI Skills Prioritization Between Instructors and Employers
snippet: Ithaka S+R released a report examining how college instructors and employers prioritize AI skills differently. The study establishes a framework of 26 AI-related skills, finding a gap between the technical proficiency employers expect and the conceptual/ethical focus instructors prioritize.
